source_text: Ἰσοστατεῖ γὰρ οὐδαμῶς, εἰς λαμπρότητα τὴν πνευματικὴν, τοῖς εὐαγγελικοῖς θεσπίσμασιν, ἡ ἐν νόμῳ σκιά· τὰ μὲν γὰρ ὅλην περιαστράπτει τὴν οἰκουμένην, ἡ δὲ ἦν μόνοις γνώρισμα τοῖς ἐξ Ἰσραήλ. {ΠΑΛΛ.} Ὀρθῶς ἔφης. {ΚΥΡ.} Ἔοικε δὲ, ὦ Παλλάδιε, καὶ ἕτερόν τι παραδηλοῦν ἡ τράπεζα καὶ ὁ λύχνος, ὁ ἔν γε τῇ πρώτῃ σκηνῇ. {ΠΑΛΛ.} Τὸ τί δὴ φής; {ΚΥΡ.} Ἰωάννην τάχα που τὸν θεσπέσιον Βαπτιστὴν ὁ λύχνος, ἄρτοι δὲ οἱ δύο καὶ δέκα, τὸν τῶν ἁγίων ἡμῖν ἀποστόλων προανατυποῦσι χορόν. {ΠΑΛΛ.} Τίνα τρόπον; {ΚΥΡ.} Ἢ οὐκ οἶσθα ὅτι τοῖς ἐν νόμῳ καὶ κατὰ τὴν Ἰουδαίαν λύχνος ἦν οἷά τις, Χριστοῦ προβαδίζων ὁ θεσπέσιος Βαπτιστὴς, καὶ περὶ αὐτοῦ προαναπεφώνηκεν ὁ Θεὸς καὶ Πατήρ· «Ἡτοίμασα λύχνον τῷ Χριστῷ μου.» Μεμαρτύρηκε δὲ τοῦτο καὶ αὐτὸς ὁ Σωτὴρ, τοῖς τῶν Ἰουδαίων καθηγηταῖς περὶ αὐτοῦ λέγων. «Ἐκεῖνος ἦν ὁ λύχνος ὁ καιόμενος καὶ φαίνων, ὑμεῖς δὲ ἠθελήσατε ἀγαλλιασθῆναι πρὸς ὥραν ἐν τῷ φωτὶ αὐτοῦ.» Θέα γὰρ ὅπως ὡς νομομαθὴς ὢν ὁ μακάριος Παῦλος, μονονουχὶ πρὸς ἀνάμνησιν ἀναφέρει λύχνου, τοῦ κατὰ τὴν πρώτην σκηνήν. Ἄσβεστον μὲν γὰρ ὁ νομοθέτης διατηρεῖσθαι δεῖν κεκέλευκεν οὕτω λέγων· «Καὶ καύσουσιν αὐτὸν Ἀαρὼν, καὶ οἱ υἱοὶ αὐτοῦ ἀπὸ ἑσπέρας ἕως πρωῒ ἐνώπιον Κυρίου ἐνδελεχῶς.» Χρόνον γε μὴν ἐπ' αὐτῷ κομιδῇ βραχὺν ἡσθέντες Ἰουδαῖοι, διά γε τὸ προσδραμεῖν τῷ δι' αὐτοῦ βαπτίσματι, καὶ θαῦμα ἑλεῖν ἐπ' αὐτῷ πολὺ, κατεκοίμισαν τῷ θανάτῳ μονονουχὶ τὸν ἀειφανῆ λύχνον κατασβεννύοντες. Εἰ γὰρ καὶ Ἡρώδου τὸ τόλμημα λέγοιτο τυχὸν, ἀλλ' οὖν ὄντος ἐξ αἵματος Ἰσραήλ· διὰ τοῦτο Χριστὸς τοῖς Ἰουδαίων λαοῖς τὸ κατὰ παντὸς ἁγίου θράσος ἐγκαλῶν, «Οὐκ ἐνδέχεται,» φησὶ, «προφήτην ἀπολέσθαι ἔξω Ἱερουσαλήμ.» {ΠΑΛΛ.} Φῶς οὖν ἄρα καὶ λύχνος, καθ' ὁμοιότητα καὶ κατὰ μέθεξιν τοῦ Χριστοῦ, καὶ ὁ θεσπέσιος Βαπτιστὴς τοῖς ἐν νόμῳ κατὰ τὴν Ἰουδαίαν. {ΚΥΡ.} Οὕτω φημί. Κατὰ τὸν ἴσον δὲ τρόπον ἄρτους νοεῖσθαί φαμεν τοὺς ἁγίους ἀποστόλους. Εἷς μὲν γὰρ ὁ φύσει τε καὶ ἀληθῶς ἄρτος ὁ ἐξ οὐρανοῦ καὶ ζωοποιός· κατὰ μίμησιν δὲ τοῦ φύσει καὶ κατὰ μέθεξιν ἄρτοι τρέφοντες εἰς εὐσέβειαν οἱ θεῖοι μυσταγωγοὶ, λόγους ἡμῖν ἐνιέντες ζωῆς, καὶ τὸν ἐκ τῆς ἀμαθίας λιμὸν, τῆς τῶν πιστευόντων ἐξιστάντες ψυχῆς. Ἰσάριθμοι δὲ τοῖς μαθηταῖς, οἱ ἄρτοι· δυοκαίδεκα γὰρ, καὶ εἰς δύο κείμενοι θέματα, ἒξ ἔνθεν, φησὶ, καὶ ἓξ ἔνθεν, μονονουχὶ καὶ ἐν κύκλῳ περιεστῶτες, καὶ ἐν μέσῳ τόπῳ κείμενον ἔχοντες ἕνα τε καὶ ἐξ οὐρανοῦ, τοῦτ' ἔστι, Χριστόν· καὶ δύο δεκάτων ἕκαστος, τοῦτ' ἔστιν, ἐκ δύο μέτρων τελείων. Τέλειοι γὰρ κατ' ἄμφω γεγόνασιν οἱ θεσπέσιοι μαθηταὶ, πρὸς πᾶν ὁτιοῦν ἀρτίως ἔχοντες ἀγαθὸν, ἔργῳ τε διαπρεπεῖς καὶ λόγῳ.
pass_a_gloss: (Cyril, continuing §15 'and the word is true') For in no way does the shadow (σκιά) in law weigh equal (ἰσοστατεῖ), unto spiritual brightness (λαμπρότης πνευματική), with the Gospel decrees (εὐαγγελικοῖς θεσπίσμασιν): for these flash round (περιαστράπτει) the whole inhabited world (οἰκουμένη), but it was a token/mark (γνώρισμα) for those from Israel alone. PALLADIUS: Rightly you spoke. CYRIL: And it seems, O Palladius, that the table and the lamp, the one at least in the first tent, also hint (παραδηλοῦν) something other. PALLADIUS: What then do you say? CYRIL: The lamp perhaps (τάχα που) [is] John the divinely-inspired (θεσπέσιος) Baptist, and the twelve loaves prefigure (προανατυποῦσι) for us the chorus/company (χορός) of the holy apostles. PALLADIUS: In what manner? CYRIL: Or do you not know that for those in law and in Judea the inspired Baptist was as it were a lamp, going ahead of (προβαδίζων) Christ, and about him God and Father proclaimed beforehand (προαναπεφώνηκεν): 'I prepared a lamp for my Christ (τῷ Χριστῷ μου).' And the Savior himself also bore witness (μεμαρτύρηκε) to this, saying about him to the leaders/teachers (καθηγηταῖς) of the Jews: 'That one was the lamp burning and shining, and you were willing to exult (ἀγαλλιασθῆναι) for an hour in his light.' For see how, being law-learned (νομομαθής), the blessed Paul all but (μονονουχί) brings back to remembrance the lamp of the first tent. For the lawgiver ordered it must be kept unquenched (ἄσβεστον), saying thus: 'And Aaron and his sons will burn it from evening until morning before the Lord continually.' But having been pleased in him for a quite short time, the Jews, through running to the baptism through him and taking much wonder at him, laid to sleep (κατεκοίμισαν) by death the ever-shining (ἀειφανῆ) lamp, all but extinguishing (κατασβεννύοντες) it. For even if the daring deed (τόλμημα) should perhaps be said to be Herod's, yet he was from the blood of Israel; for this reason Christ, charging (ἐγκαλῶν) the peoples of the Jews with the boldness (θράσος) against every holy one, 'It is not possible (οὐκ ἐνδέχεται),' he says, 'for a prophet to perish outside Jerusalem.' PALLADIUS: Light then and lamp, according to likeness (ὁμοιότης) and according to participation (μέθεξις) in Christ, was also the inspired Baptist for those in law in Judea. CYRIL: So I say. In the equal manner we say the holy apostles are to be thought loaves. For one is the bread by nature and truly, the one from heaven and life-making (ζωοποιός); but according to imitation (μίμησις) of the one by nature and according to participation, the divine initiators (μυσταγωγοί) are loaves nourishing unto godliness (εὐσέβεια), putting into us words of life, and removing (ἐξιστάντες) the famine (λιμός) from ignorance from the soul of those believing. Equal in number to the disciples [are] the loaves: for twelve, and lying in two rows, six on this side, he says, and six on that, all but standing around in a circle, and having lying in the middle place the one, also from heaven, that is, Christ; and each of two tenths, that is, from two perfect measures (μέτρων τελείων). For perfect (τέλειοι) in both have the inspired disciples become, being readily fitted (ἀρτίως ἔχοντες) for every good, conspicuous (διαπρεπεῖς) in deed (ἔργῳ) and word (λόγῳ).
pass_b_english: Cyril: …For in spiritual brightness the shadow in the law (Hebrews 10:1) is in no way equal to the decrees of the Gospel. These flash their light around the whole inhabited world, while the shadow was a token for those of Israel alone.
Cyril: It seems, Palladius, that the table and the lamp in the first tent point to something else as well.
Cyril: The lamp, perhaps, is John, the inspired Baptist, while the twelve loaves prefigure for us the company of the holy apostles.

Cyril: Or do you not know that for those under the law in Judea the inspired Baptist was a kind of lamp going before Christ, and that God the Father spoke of him beforehand: ‘I have prepared a lamp for my Christ’ (Psalm 132:17)? The Savior himself also bore witness to this, saying of him to the teachers of the Jews: ‘He was the lamp that burns and shines, and you were willing to rejoice for a while in his light’ (John 5:35). See how blessed Paul, as one learned in the law, all but calls to mind the lamp in the first tent (Hebrews 9:2). For the lawgiver commanded that it must be kept unquenched, saying: ‘And Aaron and his sons shall burn it from evening until morning before the Lord continually’ (Leviticus 24:3). Yet the Jews took delight in John for a very short time, in that they ran to the baptism he gave and marveled greatly at him; then they put the ever-shining lamp to sleep in death, all but quenching it. For even if the crime may perhaps be called Herod’s (Matthew 14:10), still he was of Israel’s blood. That is why Christ, charging the peoples of the Jews with their insolence against every holy man, says: ‘It cannot be that a prophet should perish outside Jerusalem’ (Luke 13:33).
Palladius: So the inspired Baptist too was a light and a lamp for those under the law in Judea, by likeness to Christ and by sharing in him.

Cyril: That is what I say. And in the same way we say that the holy apostles are to be understood as loaves. For only one is bread by nature and in truth: the bread that is from heaven and gives life (John 6:33). But by imitation of the one who is bread by nature, and by sharing in him, the divine guides into the mysteries are loaves that nourish us in godliness, putting into us words of life and driving the famine of ignorance out of the souls of those who believe. The loaves are equal in number to the disciples, for they are twelve, and they are laid in two rows, six on this side, it says, and six on that (Leviticus 24:6), almost as if they stood round in a circle, with the one Bread from heaven, that is, Christ, lying in the middle. And each is of two tenths (Leviticus 24:5), that is, of two perfect measures. For the inspired disciples became perfect in both respects, ready for every good thing, distinguished in deed and in word.

anf_compare.notes: No public-domain English of Cyril, De adoratione Book 10. Translated afresh from the PG 68 Greek on 2026-10-23; the withheld earlier English was not used.

apparatus.note: PG OCR; column may cut mid-sentence.

Opens mid-sentence: §15 ends 'and the statement is true', and §16 continues with γάρ, so the English begins with an ellipsis under Cyril's label. 'The shadow in the law' cited to Hebrews 10:1 ('the law has a shadow of the good things to come'). Psalm 132:17 = LXX Psalm 131:17 ('I have prepared a lamp for my Christ'). John 5:35: Cyril's 'teachers of the Jews' (καθηγηταῖς) refers to those who sent to John (John 5:33). Paul and the lamp of the first tent: Cyril treats Hebrews as Paul's; Hebrews 9:2 names 'the first tent' with its lampstand and table, the very phrase Cyril uses, so 'all but calls to mind' (μονονουχί, since Hebrews names the lampstand, λυχνία, not the lamp) is cited to Hebrews 9:2 (reviewer; replaces an earlier flag that took 'Paul' as a possible slip). The John 5:35 words are Christ's; 'burning' echoes καύσουσιν in Leviticus 24:3. Herod: allusion to the beheading of John (Matthew 14:10; also Mark 6:27); Cyril's claim that Herod was 'of Israel's blood' is kept as he states it. Luke 13:33 quoted closely. John 6:33 for 'the bread from heaven that gives life' (compare John 6:51). 'Six on this side … and six on that' with 'it says' is Cyril's paraphrase of Leviticus 24:6 (two rows of six), not the LXX wording. 'Two perfect measures' renders δύο μέτρων τελείων, kept literal because it sets up the play on 'perfect' (τέλειοι). Uncited possible echoes: 'words of life' (John 6:68; Philippians 2:16), 'famine' (Amos 8:11), 'ready for every good thing' (πρὸς πᾶν … ἀρτίως ἔχοντες ἀγαθόν; 2 Timothy 3:17 or Titus 3:1, with a play on ἄρτος / ἀρτίως that English cannot carry), 'in deed and in word' (Luke 24:19). θεσπέσιος rendered 'inspired' throughout; χορός rendered 'company'. ἕνα τε καὶ ἐξ οὐρανοῦ: masculine ἕνα takes up 'the one bread by nature' (εἷς ... ἄρτος) of the previous sentence, so rendered 'the one Bread from heaven'. διά γε τὸ προσδραμεῖν rendered 'in that they ran': it states how their brief delight showed, not its cause.

changes: Added (Hebrews 9:2) for Paul recalling the lamp of 'the first tent'; replaced the translator's textual flag (Cyril reads Hebrews as Paul's)
γνώρισμα: 'a mark known to' -> 'a token for'
'the table and the lamp, the one in the first tent' simplified
John 5:35 πρὸς ὥραν: 'for an hour' -> 'for a while'
διά γε τὸ προσδραμεῖν: removed false causal 'because'; now 'in that they ran'
'feed us toward godliness' -> 'nourish us in godliness'
Calque 'having lying in the middle place the One who is also from heaven' -> 'with the one Bread from heaven ... lying in the middle'
μέτρων τελείων: 'full measures' -> 'perfect measures' to keep Cyril's play on τέλειοι
